title: Add a fourth worked example to Motion → Trace → Shape
objective: Extend the lesson with an additional worked example that demonstrates a less common frequency ratio or phase offset, helping learners build deeper understanding.
scope: Add one new worked example to the module
Follow the existing format (title, scenario, parameters, prediction, explanation, mathematical form)
Make it testable in the interactive lab
restrictions: Do not remove or modify existing examples or exercises
Do not claim real-world physical effects without justification

inputs.name: Reference materials
inputs.source: Wolfram MathWorld and OpenStax links in the module
inputs.how_to_access: Provided in the module's sources section

deliverables.name: New worked example
deliverables.format: JSON object matching existing example structure
acceptance_criteria: Example is testable in the interactive lab
It teaches something new (not just repeating existing examples)

example_ideas: A 3:1 frequency ratio (creates a three-lobed shape)
A 3:2 frequency ratio (creates a six-pointed pattern)
A high frequency ratio like 5:2 (creates complexity)
A specific phase offset example not yet covered (e.g., 45° or 135°)
A scenario contrasting two similar phase offsets to show sensitivity
how_to_start: 1. Review the three existing worked examples. 2. Choose a frequency ratio or phase offset not yet covered. 3. Work through the math yourself. 4. Test in the interactive lab (tools/motion-trace-shape/Motion-Trace-Shape.html). 5. Write the example following the existing format. 6. Submit.
how_to_submit: Fork the repository, edit data/modules.json to add your example to the 'worked_examples' array, and open a pull request with a description of what you added.
